name: Rock-Art Sites of Tadrart Acacus
description: In the Sahara of southwestern Libya, near the Algerian border and the town of Ghat, the Acacus Mountains rise as a rugged massif of sandstone arches, caves and shelters. Thousands of paintings and engravings cover the rock, made between about 12,000 BC and AD 100. They show giraffes, elephants and herders, revealing how a once-greener land slowly turned to desert.
